newsitem.title: UK: Sierra Leone deteriorating fast, UK charities say.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone deteriorating fast, UK charities say.

text.p: British charities and aid workers on Friday warned that conditions were deteriorating rapidly in Sierra Leone.
They said thousands of refugees were fleeing the West African nation after a May 25 coup in which a military junta seized power. Those left faced soaring prices, food shortages and reduced harvests.

"The recent coup and subsequent instability has increased the suffering of the poorest people in Sierra Leone," a group of charities, including Actionaid, Oxfam and Save the Children Fund, said in a statement.
Charity staff working in the country reported many of the classic early warning signs of a serious humanitarian emergency, it said.
The charities said over 30,000 refugees had fled to neighbouring states with about 50,000 combatants ranging across the country. Rice, palm oil and cassava prices had risen 100 percent.
"We are deeply concerned that a serious emergency is rapidly developing," said one aid worker speaking from Sierra Leone.
"What is needed now is immediate humanitarian assistance and an end to the political stand-off and violence. Sierra Leone needs help and not political posturing," the worker added.
